entries.summary: Both Greta hands begin with a loose 1-7 run in one suit; their honour structures are different.
entries.whatItIs: A learner family linking two T&M specials that share the same seven-tile suited run but complete the hand with different Wind/Dragon requirements.
entries.whatItMeans: The 1-7 run is the common visual cue. Greta's Dragon adds all four Winds and a Dragon Pung/Kong; Greta's Garden instead adds all four Winds and all three Dragons as single honours.
entries.whySpecial: The same suited seven-tile backbone leads to two materially different special hands depending on how the seven remaining honour tiles are organised.

variants.definition: A 1-7 run in one suit, all four Winds and a Dragon Pung/Kong.

variants.label: Greta's Garden
variants.definition: A 1-7 run in one suit plus all four Winds and all three Dragons.

entries.summary: A 1-9 run in one suit, one of each Dragon and a Wind pair.
entries.whatItIs: An irregular Western special joining a complete suited straight to all three Dragon identities and a pair of Winds.
entries.whatItMeans: The nine suited tiles are singles forming 1 through 9; the remaining five tiles are the three Dragons plus two identical Winds.
entries.whySpecial: It combines a complete one-suit straight with both Dragon and Wind honour structures without using normal meld decomposition.

entries.whySpecial: Its qualification is a specific two-suit arrangement rather than a general family of melds.

entries.summary: Confused Gates, Golden Gates and Dragon's Gates share a name theme but have materially different structures.
entries.whatItIs: A disambiguation topic for three T&M specials whose names contain Gates.
entries.whatItMeans: This topic exists to help a learner distinguish names, not to assert a common canonical hand. Confused Gates uses a 2-8 run plus terminal Pungs; Golden Gates uses even-rank pairs plus a terminal and corresponding Dragon; Dragon's Gates combines a 2-8 run/pair with a terminal meld and corresponding Dragon meld.
entries.whySpecial: Name similarity is unusually likely to cause lookup mistakes here, while the underlying predicates are different.

variants.label: Dragon's Gates

entries.referenceNote: Do not merge any of these with Gates of Heaven from name similarity; the #351 Gates family remains a separate structural relationship.

entries.summary: One suit, four melds and a pair; at most one meld may be a Chow under this Western calculated treatment.
entries.whatItIs: A Thompson & Maloney calculated one-suit treatment rather than a fixed-value special.
entries.whatItMeans: The hand stays within one suit and uses a normal grouped structure; unlike the British authored Purity guidance, this profile's executable treatment permits one Chow.
entries.whySpecial: It is an important boundary between fixed special-hand entries and calculated profile scoring, and it demonstrates that the same display name can hide structural differences across rules.
entries.referenceNote: Score and exposure adjustment must be rendered from the calculated exact treatment; do not invent a fixed winner/fishing value. A concrete visual should be generated from the canonical predicate during implementation rather than reusing British Purity unchanged.

entries.whatItIs: A learner family linking two fixed Western specials that use one non-terminal Pung/Kong in every suit plus a specific honour meld/pair combination.
entries.whatItMeans: Sunrise uses East Wind as the meld and White Dragon as the pair; Sunset uses White Dragon as the meld and Red Dragon as the pair.
entries.whySpecial: The suited skeleton is shared while the two honour roles create distinct named hands.

entries.summary: Three related hands share a complete 1-9 suited run; the honour Pung/Kong and pair determine which hand it is.
entries.whatItIs: A learner family for Guardian Winds, Guardian Dragons and Dragon's Tail.
entries.whatItMeans: Guardian Winds uses a Wind meld and Wind pair; Guardian Dragons uses a Dragon meld and Dragon pair; Dragon's Tail deliberately mixes the honour families, one as the meld and the other as the pair.
entries.whySpecial: The same complete suited sequence supports three named treatments through different honour-family constraints.

entries.summary: Chinese Odds and Odds & Evens both make tile-number parity part of qualification, but they use different structures.
entries.whatItIs: A browse family for Western hands whose defining rule is based on odd/even suited ranks.
entries.whatItMeans: Chinese Odds is a normal grouped one-suit Pung/Kong hand using odd ranks. Odds & Evens distributes odd ranks across two suits and even ranks across the third in its own complete predicate.
entries.whySpecial: The rank parity itself, rather than only suits or honour families, is a core qualification rule.
